Rachel —

Thanks for the quick demos last week. As discussed with our procurement and privacy teams, please find attached our redline of the standard Redwood DPA (Solaire_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf). The items we care most about:

- TRAINING / MODEL IMPROVEMENT: We need an explicit prohibition on using Customer Data to train or improve models. Proposed language in the redline (Section 2.4): “Customer Data shall not be used to train, tune, or improve any model or machine learning system, nor to create derivative models, unless Customer provides prior written consent.”
- SUBPROCESSORS: Prior notice and a 30-day window to object for new subprocessors that will process Customer Data; automatic termination right if objection is reasonable and unresolved.
- DATA TRANSFERS: We require SCCs (if EU data) and a statement that EU personal data will not be transferred outside the EU without either SCCs or Customer approval.
- LOGS & RETENTION: No retention of logs containing PII beyond 90 days unless required by law.

We’d like to execute via DocuSign — please return any Redwood redlines by EOD Thursday so we can keep schedule for a Dec 1 kickoff.

Attachments: Solaire_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf

Best,

We can offer the carve-out plus an explicit exception for aggregated, de-identified telemetry and platform performance metrics.

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed Solaire's redline and drafted a focused response (attached: Redwood_DPA_Response_v2.pdf). High-level counsel position: we can agree to a strong customer-protective training carve-out with limited exceptions that preserve Redwood's ability to operate and secure the platform. Suggested language (clean copy):

"Customer Data will not be used to train, tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models or create derivative models ("Training Use"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may process aggregated and de-identified metrics that do not and cannot reasonably be re-associated with a customer or individual for the purpose of improving the Redwood service ("Aggregated Metrics"). Aggregated Metrics will exclude raw Customer Data and Personal Data as defined in the DPA."

Notes/risks: the exception for Aggregated Metrics is intentionally narrow — it allows platform-level telemetry (latency, batch sizes, cache hit rates) but excludes text/content used by the customer. If Solaire insists on an absolute prohibition (no exceptions), we should get explicit acknowledgement that Redwood may still process telemetry and a carve-in for security/abuse detection as required by law.

On subprocessors: propose notice and a 30-day review period for new subprocessors that will have access to unredacted Customer Data; for lower-risk subprocessors (hosting, CDN), provide notice only. This balances customer control and operational agility.

On retention: recommend we counter with 120 days for logs containing PII but commit to shorter retention for high-sensitivity PII and an export option on termination. 90 days is on the conservative side and will add operational overhead.

If the team is aligned, I recommend sending the attached PDF to Solaire with these three points called out in short bullets and proposing DocuSign for signatures. Alex, can you confirm there are no further legal flags on the Aggregated Metrics phrasing?

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
